Subject: Multiparametric MRI Prostate | Bravis Ziekenhuis | 05 Feb 2025

Clinical context: 57-year-old male, PSA 6.9 ng/mL, prior biopsy positive for ISUP GG 1. Re-evaluation for biopsy decision.

FINDINGS: Prostate volume 77.9 mL. The gland is symmetrically enlarged with a prominent transitional zone and mild median lobe hypertrophy. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates preserved zonal anatomy without focal hypointense lesions. DWI shows no restricted diffusion. DCE is negative for early focal enhancement. No suspicious PI-RADS 3 or higher lesion is identified. The peripheral zone appears unremarkable. The prostate occupies the expected pelvic location, measuring approximately 58 mm craniocaudal, 62 mm transverse, and 44 mm anteroposterior.

IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 2. Benign prostatic enlargement with no suspicious focal lesion identified. PSAD 0.089 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.49575716.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: The patient was seen today for routine health maintenance and discussion of his initial PSA screening results. His baseline PSA was recorded at 2.0 ng/mL, which falls within the acceptable range for his age group. Current lower urinary tract symptoms were noted during the consultation.
